title: Power lifting of invariants gives an adequate affine quotient
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and $G$ a smooth affine group scheme of finite type over $k$. Suppose that for every equivariant surjection $B\twoheadrightarrow C$ of finitely generated commutative $k$-algebras with rational $G$-actions and every $c\in C^G$, there are $N>0$ and $b\in B^G$ mapping to $c^N$. Rational action means a coordinate coaction satisfying counit and coassociativity, and $B^G$ is the equalizer of that coaction and $b\mapsto b\otimes1$. Then, for every finitely generated commutative $k$-algebra $E$ with rational $G$-action, the canonical morphism $[\operatorname{Spec}E/G]\to\operatorname{Spec}(E^G)$ is an adequate moduli space [def-sfb-adequate-moduli-space]. The quotient stack and the canonical morphism have the conventions of [def-sfb-affine-action-quotient-stack, lem-sfb-affine-action-stack-presentation].

source.place: Lemma 9.2.5 (3-prime and 3-double-prime), Remark 9.2.4 (1) over a field, Lemma 9.2.8 (3), and Theorem 9.1.4 with Remark 9.1.5. Finite-type power-lifting criterion followed by affine GIT. Read arXiv:1005.2398v3 online; local PDF WANTED.

proof.text: First extend the assumed power lifting to all rational $G$-algebras, without finite-generation hypotheses. Let $u:B\twoheadrightarrow C$ be such a surjection and $c\in C^G$. Put $H=k[G]$ and choose a preimage $x\in B$. By [lem-sfb-comodule-finite-subrepresentation], a finite-dimensional rational submodule $V\subset B$ contains $x$. Let $B_0=k[V]\subset B$ and $C_0=u(B_0)\subset C$. A basis of $V$ generates $B_0$, and its images generate $C_0$, so both are finitely generated $k$-algebras. Since the coaction is multiplicative and preserves $V$, it preserves $B_0$, and equivariance makes $C_0$ a rational subalgebra: for $y=u(z)$ with $z\in B_0$, $\rho_C(y)=(u\otimes1)\rho_B(z)$ belongs to $C_0\otimes_kH$; its inclusion into $C\otimes_kH$ is injective, so the restricted coaction identities hold there. Moreover $c\in C_0^G$: the equality $\rho_C(c)=c\otimes1$ restricts to $C_0$, since $C_0\otimes_kH\to C\otimes_kH$ is injective (extend a $k$-basis of $C_0$ to one of $C$). Apply the hypothesis to the surjection $B_0\twoheadrightarrow C_0$ and the element $c$. Its invariant lift of $c^N$ is also invariant in $B$. This proves the extension for arbitrary $B,C$.

source.place: Lemma 9.2.5, finite-type condition (3-prime) to (3), specialized to a field; finite-subcomodule reduction spelled out using Milne Proposition 4.7.

proof.text: Fix $E$ as in the statement and put $R=E^G$, $\mathcal X=[\operatorname{Spec}E/G]$, $Y=\operatorname{Spec}R$. Use [def-sfb-affine-action-quotient-stack] with its left torsors, pullback arrows, total-arrow composition and canonical atlas; pass from right coordinate coactions to left scheme actions by group inversion, as specified in the descent lemma. The canonical $\phi:\mathcal X\to Y$ is the one of [lem-sfb-affine-action-stack-presentation]. Apply [lem-sfb-affine-action-quasicoherent-descent] to $D=E$, $A=R$ and the invariant inclusion $R\hookrightarrow E$: it gives quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness of $\phi$. For every $R$-algebra $L$, its base change has the action-quotient presentation $\mathcal X_L\simeq[\operatorname{Spec}E_L/G]$, where $E_L=E\otimes_RL$, and the stated descent and section identifications apply even if $L$ or subsequent algebras are not finitely generated.

source.place: Theorem 9.1.4 and Remark 9.1.5, affine action presentation; descent expanded via Stacks Tag 06WT.

proof.text: Let $W=\operatorname{Spec}L\to Y$ be any etale affine map. Take any surjection $\mathcal A\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal B$ of quasi-coherent algebras on $\mathcal X_W$, including algebras that do not descend from $\mathcal X$, and any $t\in\Gamma(\mathcal X_W,\mathcal B)$. By [lem-sfb-affine-action-quasicoherent-descent] this is a surjection $B\twoheadrightarrow C$ of equivariant $E_L$-algebras and an element $t\in C^G$. Forgetting the $E_L$-algebra structures leaves rational $G$-algebras over $k$, so step 1 gives $N>0$ and $b\in B^G$ mapping to $t^N$. The same descent identification, compatible with the algebra map, turns $b$ into $s\in\Gamma(\mathcal X_W,\mathcal A)$ mapping to $t^N$. Thus the required local power lifting holds on every such $W$.

source.place: Theorem 9.1.4, proof, expanded directly on arbitrary etale affine charts using Section 2.1 and Lemma 9.2.5 (3).

proof.text: It remains to check the structure-sheaf isomorphism, rather than infer it merely from equality of global sections on $Y$. For the same etale $R$-algebra $L$, [lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-flat] says that $L$ is flat over $R$. Set $H=k[G]$ and let $\delta:E\to E\otimes_kH$ be the $R$-linear map $e\mapsto\rho_E(e)-e\otimes1$. For $r\in R$ one has $\rho_E(re)=(r\otimes1)\rho_E(e)$, hence $\delta(re)=r\delta(e)$, using the first-factor $R$-action on $E\otimes_kH$. By definition $0\to R\to E\xrightarrow{\delta}E\otimes_kH$ is exact. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact] to tensor this sequence with $L$ over $R$. Under the canonical associativity identification $(E\otimes_kH)\otimes_RL\simeq(E\otimes_RL)\otimes_kH$, if $\rho_E(e)=\sum_i e_i\otimes h_i$, the resulting map is $\delta_L(e\otimes l)=\sum_i(e_i\otimes l)\otimes h_i-(e\otimes l)\otimes1$; this is exactly the difference of the coaction and the trivial map for $E_L$. Its kernel is therefore $E_L^G$, and exactness identifies it with $L$ via $l\mapsto1\otimes l$. By [lem-sfb-affine-action-quasicoherent-descent], these are precisely $\Gamma(W,\mathcal O_Y)$ and $\Gamma(\mathcal X_W,\mathcal O_{\mathcal X_W})$, and this identification is the structural map, naturally in $W$. Thus $\mathcal O_Y\to\phi_*\mathcal O_{\mathcal X}$ is an isomorphism on the affine objects of the small etale site, hence an isomorphism of sheaves.

source.place: Theorem 9.1.4, structure-sheaf clause, expanded as flat base change of the invariant equalizer; Definition 5.1.1.

proof.text: Step 2 supplies the quasi-compact, quasi-separated canonical morphism from the algebraic quotient stack. Step 3 supplies condition (2) of [def-sfb-adequate-moduli-space], including all quasi-coherent algebras on every etale affine base change; step 4 supplies its condition (1), the canonical structural-sheaf isomorphism. Thus both numbered conditions, together with the qc/qs hypotheses, hold, and $\phi$ is an adequate moduli space.
